question.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for the integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(b-a)f(c) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{1-0}{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{1}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1}[(\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+1))-(\operatorname{ln}⁡(0+1))] \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ \frac{1}{c+1} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ c+1 & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)} \\ c & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}-1\end{aligned}
$$
